persona: Faisal Baig, 31, indie game developer in Karachi who runs the two-person studio Paperkite and is fighting a rent hike from his landlord

messages.text: need help writing a reply to my landlord, im so annoyed. Tariq Mirza (he owns my flat) sent a notice saying rent goes to 60k from 1 April. i want to push back politely but firmly

Happy to help. A firm but polite structure works well: thank him for the notice, acknowledge the increase, ask him to justify it with comparable rents in your area, propose a smaller revision phased in over time, and ask for a fresh agreement in writing. You could even suggest 50,000 a month as your counter-offer. Want me to draft it?
yes pls. i have to send it by the 10th or the offer to negotiate lapses. also my cousin Hamza Malik is a property lawyer btw

Draft: "Dear Mr Mirza, thank you for your notice dated 28 February. I value our tenancy and wish to continue it, but the proposed increase is well above what comparable flats in the area are asking. Could you share the basis for the figure? I would like to propose a smaller, phased revision and a fresh written agreement. Kind regards." I can make it shorter or firmer if you like.
50k is too low, he'll laugh. if he doesnt budge i might just move to Bahria Town honestly. also he gave me a rent portal login, password is hunter22, dont put that in the letter obviously 😅

Understood, I'll leave the password out entirely and keep the letter free of any counter-figure for now, so you can decide on a number after seeing his justification. If he refuses to explain the increase, you can escalate in your next letter.

messages.text: random q, for a top-down delivery game is A* or Dijkstra better for npc pathing on a tile grid? the tiles have different movement costs (mud slows you down)

A* is usually the better choice when each NPC has a single destination. It uses a heuristic to steer the search toward the goal, so it expands far fewer tiles than Dijkstra, and it handles weighted tiles like mud just fine as long as the heuristic never overestimates the remaining cost. Dijkstra is better when you need distances to many targets at once, for example a flow field that many NPCs share.
ok A* it is. what heuristic should i use if diagonal moves are allowed?

Use octile distance: with dx and dy as the absolute differences, take the larger one plus about 0.41 times the smaller one, scaled by your cheapest tile cost. That keeps it admissible. If you want to stay safe, use the minimum movement cost across all tile types as the scale factor.
thanks. my brain is fried, between the landlord and this build i might as well live in a tent on Clifton beach 😂
That sounds exhausting. A short break after you get the pathing working might help, and the heuristic is a small change once the grid code exists. Good luck with the build.
